monitor.published_by: CBOE, published daily and distributed through FRED as VXVCLS and VIXCLS
monitor.variable: VIX3M minus VIX, the term structure slope

net_level.claimed: the net return of holding SVXY continuously over the window, after execution costs, rather than a difference between two groups of days

payer.who: buyers of VIX futures and index options -- portfolio managers and dealers purchasing protection against equity drawdowns
payer.why_they_keep_paying: they are buying insurance against losses they are mandated or unwilling to bear, and insurance that is not priced above its expected cost would not be written by anyone; the premium is the price of that transfer rather than a mistake being made

required_effect.plausibility_source: published estimates of the roll-yield harvest on short VIX futures run roughly 0.5 to 1.0 before catastrophic tail events; 0.60 is the CONSERVATIVE end of that range and not its midpoint, and the -0.5x structure dilutes leverage without changing a ratio, though its daily rebalancing drag is not in the estimate

pre_declarations.source: answered in writing before any bar of SVXY was captured; the monitor's availability and inversion frequency were measured first, which is a fact about the monitor and never about the position's returns

window.adverse_episode: March 2020, when VIX reached 82 and the term structure inverted on 53 days of that year, plus the 2025 spike with 29 inverted days

monitor.published_by: CBOE publishes VIX daily and FRED distributes it as VIXCLS, while realised volatility is computed from index prices
monitor.variable: VIX minus the 21-day realised volatility of the S&P 500

net_level.claimed: the net return of holding XYLD continuously over the window, after execution costs and with its expense ratio already inside its price, rather than a difference between two groups of days

payer.who: buyers of S&P 500 call options, who pay for upside exposure that the fund sells them inside the wrapper
payer.why_they_keep_paying: they want convex upside at limited cost, and structured product issuers hedge by buying calls, so demand for upside is not sensitive to price; the premium is what the sellers earn for taking the other side of that demand and for bearing the crash risk it implies

required_effect.plausibility_source: published studies of the buy-write index find a Sharpe roughly equal to or modestly above the underlying over long samples; the range is recalled, wide, and sits below the S&P 500 own at the low end for the fund fee and the capped upside, and the conservative end is below the bar

pre_declarations.source: answered in writing before any bar of XYLD was captured; the monitor trigger frequency was measured first, which is a fact about the monitor and never about the fund's returns

window.adverse_episode: February 2018, when VIX more than doubled in a day, March 2020, and the 2022 drawdown
window.why_shorter_than_available: the dataset contract needs two warmup rows and one forward row, so three of the 2702 bars the feed serves cannot be evaluated

monitor.published_by: CBOE publishes VXN daily and FRED distributes it as VXNCLS, while realised volatility is computed from index prices
monitor.variable: VXN minus the 21-day realised volatility of the Nasdaq-100

net_level.claimed: the net return of holding QYLD continuously over the window, after execution costs and with its expense ratio already inside its price, rather than a difference between two groups of days

payer.who: buyers of Nasdaq-100 call options, who pay for upside exposure that the fund sells them inside the wrapper
payer.why_they_keep_paying: they want convex upside at limited cost, and structured product issuers hedge by buying calls, so demand for upside is not sensitive to price; the premium is what the sellers earn for taking the other side of that demand and for bearing the crash risk it implies

required_effect.plausibility_source: published studies of the Nasdaq-100 buy-write index find a Sharpe below the index own over long samples, because the call overlay caps a strongly trending upside; the range is recalled and wide, and its conservative end is below the bar of 0.500

pre_declarations.source: answered in writing before any bar of QYLD was captured, from a monitor fixed by the family and not by this fund

window.adverse_episode: March 2020, and the 2022 drawdown, which was deeper for the Nasdaq-100 than for the S&P 500
window.why_shorter_than_available: the dataset contract needs two warmup rows and one forward row, so three of the 2702 bars the feed serves cannot be evaluated
